persona: Independent simulated first-time RILL beginner interested in a short ambient soundtrack sketch.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: I completed naming, VST assignment, notes, audio stretch, mixing, saving and both export commands with the mouse. Precise note placement and duration correction took extra steps.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark interface, teal waveforms, colored notes and tall Mixer strips looked coherent and readable. The many toolbar controls felt dense.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most buttons and mixer drags responded promptly. Preparing audio, one output-stream failure, export progress, and initially black native file dialogs interrupted the flow. This is a session impression, not a hardware benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: The visible hints and labeled Mixer buttons helped. I had to translate 30 seconds into beats, several drawn note starts were staggered despite similar drag starts, and playback failed once without an immediately clear cause.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The requested mouse controls, native VST3 assignment, audio stretching, bus/send routing and WAV/MIDI exports were discoverable. I did not evaluate other plug-ins or advanced sound design.

findings.observation: File > Rename project exposed an on-screen Keyboard. Clicking Clear and letters let me apply the chosen name mist without physical keyboard input.
The visible Double-click for MIDI hint led to the Device library, where Rill Lab Sine was listed as a VST3 instrument. Assign instrument produced a MIDI track and pattern.

Clip Properties provided a numeric keypad. Setting 56 beats at 112 BPM showed 30 seconds. Choosing Stretch and entering 56 beats extended the startup audio to 350%, with an explicit 0:30.000 endpoint.

Pencil drags created twelve sustained notes, but several starts appeared at different times despite drags beginning at the same intended x positions. The last drags extended the clip to 0:30.134. I reset duration from 56.25 to 56 beats using Properties; the final project header returned to 0:30.000.
Mixer faders and pan knobs gave immediate numeric feedback. Audio ended at -14.0 dB / L20 and MIDI at -9.1 dB / R20. Mute and Solo each showed an active highlight and were switched off again.
Add bus immediately created New bus. MIDI Add send opened Routing; + Send offered New bus, and choosing it displayed a 0.25x Post send. Later the mixer showed Bus 1 in and Send - New bus.
After an earlier loop playback had advanced transport numbers, a later playback attempt stopped with Audio output stream failed or disconnected. No heard-audio claim was made.
A subsequent Play retry advanced the transport to 004.03.23 and showed green MIDI, bus and master meter activity, with master reading -17.5 dB. I then stopped playback.
The native save/export dialogs initially appeared as a black rectangle; a later screenshot showed usable file pickers. Their default names already matched mist, allowing mouse-only acceptance.

The save dialog accepted mist.rill in session-4 and the title lost its unsaved dot. WAV export showed Arrangement 0:30 after disabling effect tails. MIDI showed Exported - mist.mid, and Recent exports listed both mist.mid and mist.wav under Completed exports.

outcome.status: Completed through the visible UI: a named 30-second audio-plus-VST-MIDI arrangement was saved, both export commands completed according to Recent exports, and all requested mixer controls were exercised. File contents remain independently unverified.
outcome.composition: Startup Circuit rhythm audio stretched to 30 seconds at 350%, plus a 56-beat MIDI pattern with twelve sustained notes in four rough chord groups (C4/E4/G4, A3/C4/E4, F3/A3/C4, G3/B3/D4). Some note starts are staggered. Audio is quieter and left-panned; MIDI is right-panned and has a 0.25x post send to New bus.
outcome.playback_observed: Initial loop playback advanced transport numbers but the captured meters were dark. A later attempt displayed Audio output stream failed or disconnected. Retrying Play subsequently advanced to 004.03.23 with active MIDI, bus and master meters and a -17.5 dB master reading. Playback was stopped before final.png.

limitations: No file contents or heard audio were verified; independent coordinator verification follows.

The WAV transient success toast was not observed: export progress was seen, and the Completed exports submenu later explicitly listed WAV - mist.wav. The false toast flag does not mean export failure.
The project path comes from the visible save dialog and removal of the unsaved title dot; no file inspection was used.
Virtual audio sink and software graphics may affect this session. No physical-hardware latency, audio quality, or other VST compatibility claim is made.
The musical balance was selected using visible control values; it was not evaluated by listening.
Elapsed interaction includes screenshots, tool overhead and reporting and is not a speed benchmark.

mixer_outcome.volume: Dragged the Circuit drums fader from -6.0 dB to -14.0 dB and New instrument from -2.5 dB to -9.1 dB; numeric values visibly updated.
mixer_outcome.pan: Dragged audio pan knob left to L20 and MIDI pan knob right to R20; both labels visibly updated.
mixer_outcome.mute: Clicked Circuit drums Mute during playback; orange active highlight appeared. Clicked again to restore unmuted state.
mixer_outcome.solo: Clicked New instrument Solo during playback; active highlight appeared. Clicked again to clear solo before export.
mixer_outcome.bus: Clicked Mixer Add bus; a New bus strip appeared with 0.0 dB fader and Master output. Final mixer displayed Bus 1 in.
mixer_outcome.send: Clicked MIDI Add send, then + Send, then New bus. Routing displayed New bus, 0.25x level and Post selected; final mixer displayed Send - New bus.
